solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Richard at home with child and American poet (9)

blocks.note: Dick is the short form of Richard

annotation.surface: A family portrait: Richard at home with the kids and a visiting American poet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface lists four people; really Richard, home and child build one surname, and only 'American poet' is a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Emily Dickinson is the celebrated nineteenth-century American poet.

entries.clue: Plays dumb at first with Hindu deity (5)

indicatorNotes.at first: take only the first letter of 'dumb'

annotation.surface: Someone feigns stupidity at first before a Hindu god comes on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plays dumb' reads as one phrase, but 'Plays' is the definition on its own and 'dumb' only lends its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Drama is plays collectively, as in a course on modern drama.

entries.clue: Arrest fool following tip in Berlin landmark (10,7)

blocks.note: to check is to arrest or halt
the tip of a pencil is its point
a charlie is a fool in British slang

annotation.surface: A police arrest of an idiot, acting on a tip-off, somewhere in Berlin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a tip-off to the police; it is a point. Charlie as a fool is British slang: 'a right charlie'.
annotation.definitionFit: Checkpoint Charlie was the best-known crossing point in the Berlin Wall, now a tourist site.

entries.clue: International rambler and rock enthusiast is retiring (11)

blocks.note: Int. is the abbreviation of international
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British rock-and-roll fan

annotation.surface: A globe-trotting hiker who loves rock climbing is stepping back from it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock enthusiast' suggests a climber or geologist; it is a Teddy boy, the 1950s British youth cult devoted to rock and roll.
annotation.definitionFit: Retiring and introverted both describe someone shy who keeps to themselves.

entries.clue: Twisted edges of large cutting tool (6)

blocks.note: a twisted mind is a sick one
L and E, the outer letters of large

annotation.surface: The warped rim of a big blade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' looks like an anagram signal, but here it means sick, as in a twisted sense of humour.
annotation.definitionFit: A sickle is a curved hand blade for cutting crops.

entries.clue: Pardon me starting to brag about famous connections (4-4)

indicatorNotes.starting: to start is to jump or jerk, so the letters are jolted into a new order

annotation.surface: An apology before launching into boasts about the celebrities one knows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starting to' reads as 'beginning to', but 'starting' is the jolt that rearranges the letters. The surface is apt: name-droppers often open with a false 'pardon me'.
annotation.definitionFit: To name-drop is to mention famous acquaintances casually to impress.

entries.clue: Girl group about to be entertained by bad actor (5)

indicatorNotes.to be entertained by: RE is taken in, hosted, inside HAM

blocks.note: a ham is an over-the-top actor

annotation.surface: A pop girl band is about to be put up by a terrible actor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Girl group' suggests a pop band; it is a harem. 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' gives RE and 'to be entertained by' is the containment.
annotation.definitionFit: A harem is the group of wives or women in a household, hence a girl group.

entries.clue: Streaker seen regularly in hospital passageways to arrive on time? (7,5)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across-style reading, one thing on another follows it, so T is tacked on after COME

blocks.note: H is the map symbol for hospital

annotation.surface: A naked runner keeps turning up in hospital corridors, hoping to be punctual.
annotation.walkthrough: The streaker is not a naked sports fan but a comet streaking across the sky, seen every 76 years or so.
annotation.definitionFit: Halley's Comet streaks across the sky and returns on a regular cycle of about 76 years.

entries.clue: Device for cooking Indian bread’s run short (10)

blocks.note: roti is an Indian flatbread; the ’s adds S
a run is a series, cut short to SERIE

annotation.surface: A gadget for making Indian bread has run low.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run short' reads as 'running out'; really 'run' is a series (a run of wins) and 'short' clips its final S.
annotation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a rotating spit for roasting meat.

entries.clue: Wooden leg mostly underneath chart (5)

indicatorNotes.underneath: in a down answer LE sits beneath MAP

annotation.surface: A pirate's peg leg tucked mostly under a sea chart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wooden leg' reads as a peg leg, but 'Wooden' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Maple is used as an adjective for things made of that wood, as in a maple floor.

entries.clue: Set sail towards south-east, invading Indian territory (2,2,3)

indicatorNotes.invading: an invader pushes into territory, so TOSE pushes into the middle of GOA

blocks.note: Goa, a state on India's west coast

annotation.surface: A fleet sets off south-east to invade part of India.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a naval invasion; the invading is only letters going into GOA.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a ship that sets sail puts out from port onto the open water.

entries.clue: Presenter with temperature wearing dress in deserted location (5,4)

indicatorNotes.wearing: HOST and T sit inside the dress GOWN, as a body inside clothes

blocks.note: a TV presenter is a host

annotation.surface: A feverish TV presenter wearing a frock turns up somewhere abandoned.
annotation.walkthrough: The gown is opened after its first letter, G, and HOST plus T go in.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive: an abandoned mining or boom town, empty but for its buildings, is the classic deserted location.

entries.clue: Start decree spreading proprietary information (5,6)

indicatorNotes.spreading: the letters are spread out and rearranged

annotation.surface: An official edict begins leaking a company's confidential know-how.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like a verb commanding the decree; it is only letters in the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: A trade secret is confidential business information a firm owns, such as a recipe.

entries.clue: Rascal to swindle leader of Poland (5)

indicatorNotes.leader of: take the first letter of Poland

annotation.surface: A villain plans to con the Polish head of state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leader of Poland' suggests a president; it is simply the letter P.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually said fondly of a naughty child.

entries.clue: Noodle dish dropping right on American god (4-2)

indicatorNotes.dropping: in this down answer the R of RAMEN drops from the top to the bottom

blocks.note: RAMEN with its R (right) moved down to the end

annotation.surface: A bowl of noodles that has lost its dressing is offered to a US deity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' usually means losing a letter; here the R drops down the column to the end instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Amen-Ra is the ancient Egyptian king of the gods, Amun fused with the sun god Ra.

entries.clue: Stop antagonistic French inspector getting decapitated (5)

indicatorNotes.getting decapitated: JAVERT loses its head, the first letter

blocks.note: Inspector Javert, antagonist of Les Misérables, minus J

annotation.surface: Preventing a hostile French detective from being guillotined.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Antagonistic' is not an adjective of mood: Javert is literally the antagonist of Victor Hugo's Les Misérables.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of heading something off before it happens, as in averting disaster.

entries.clue: California sailor missing at Arthur’s Seat? (7)

indicatorNotes.missing: a sailor missing from his post is absent, so the AT is absent from MATELOT

blocks.note: CA is the US state abbreviation
a matelot is a sailor, with AT removed

annotation.surface: A Californian sailor fails to turn up at Arthur's Seat, the hill above Edinburgh.
annotation.walkthrough: Arthur's Seat is an Edinburgh hill, so the question mark flags a pun: Camelot was King Arthur's seat of court. Matelot is British slang for sailor.
annotation.definitionFit: Camelot was the legendary castle and court from which King Arthur ruled.

entries.clue: Spread stone on buttress (9)

blocks.note: a prop is a support or buttress

annotation.surface: Laying stone over a supporting wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like part of the building job, as in spreading mortar, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as when rumours or ideas are propagated; gardeners also propagate plants to spread them.

entries.clue: Recognise air conditioning geek overturning shelf (11)

indicatorNotes.overturning: WONK is turned round to KNOW

blocks.note: a wonk is a geek, reversed

annotation.surface: A nerd tips over a shelf while fixing the air conditioning.
annotation.walkthrough: A wonk is a studious geek, a word more common in American English (a policy wonk).
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of admitting or accepting, as in recognising someone's rights.

entries.clue: Vegetable we put in sink before shower (5,6)

indicatorNotes.put in: what is put in something ends up inside it, so WE ends up inside SET

blocks.note: to pepper is to shower, as with bullets

annotation.surface: A cook drops a vegetable into the kitchen sink before taking a shower.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sink' and 'shower' both look like bathroom fittings; each is a verb here, to set and to pepper.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the mild capsicum, called a bell pepper in America, is cooked and eaten as a vegetable.

entries.clue: Mineral found in farm building’s floor (6)

indicatorNotes.found in: a thing found in a place lies inside it, so ORE lies inside STY

blocks.note: a sty is a pigs' building on a farm

annotation.surface: Some mineral turned up in the pigsty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Floor' looks like the floor of the sty; it is a level of a building. Storey is the British spelling of story.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the third floor and the third storey are the same level; storey is the British spelling of story.

entries.clue: Fixes cutting room for low rate? (6,4)

indicatorNotes.cutting: a blade cutting something goes into it, so NAILS goes into SPACE

blocks.note: to nail is to fix in place

annotation.surface: A handyman fixing up a room offers a discount.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low rate' suggests a cheap price; the question mark signals it means very slow speed.
annotation.definitionFit: A snail's pace is a very slow speed, a low rate of progress.

entries.clue: Go without military clothing in speech? (8)

indicatorNotes.in speech: the phrase is heard, not spelt

annotation.surface: Choosing to give up army uniform, when you talk about it.
annotation.walkthrough: The force here is the armed forces, and wear is clothing as in menswear.
annotation.definitionFit: Forswear means to renounce, literally to swear off, so what you forswear you then go without.

entries.clue: Hotel guest to dislike carrying passport, say (8)

indicatorNotes.carrying: whoever carries something holds it within, so RESENT holds ID

blocks.note: a passport is one form of ID

annotation.surface: A hotel guest who hates having to show a passport at check-in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the passport as just one example of ID.
annotation.definitionFit: A hotel's residents are the guests staying there.

entries.clue: Loads of old sponges perhaps abandoned by front of loo (6)

indicatorNotes.abandoned by: CLEANS loses L, the front of loo

blocks.clueFragment: sponges perhaps abandoned by front of loo
blocks.note: sponges = cleans, without L, the first letter of loo

annotation.surface: Heaps of ancient bath sponges left behind by the toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sponges' reads as a plural noun; it is a verb, cleans. 'Loads of' is the definition with its link: oceans of time.
annotation.definitionFit: Oceans, informally, means loads, as in oceans of room.

entries.clue: Without conditions, like useless guitar? (2,7,8)

blocks.note: the idiom for an unconditional offer
read literally: a guitar with no strings on it cannot be played

annotation.surface: A free gift offered like a guitar that cannot be played.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading of the idiom.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from strings tied to a gift, and literally true of a guitar with no strings fitted, which is useless.

entries.clue: Plaster company supports upcoming reductions (6)

indicatorNotes.supports: in a down answer CO sits under STUC, holding it up
indicatorNotes.upcoming: in a down answer CUTS reads upwards

annotation.surface: A plastering firm backs the spending cuts that are on the way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming' looks like 'imminent'; in a down clue it means coming up the column.
annotation.definitionFit: Stucco is a plaster used to coat walls.

entries.clue: She briefly appeared, dancing with a certain figure (4-6)

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancers move all over the floor, so the letters move out of their order

annotation.surface: A woman makes a short guest appearance, dancing, and shows off her figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Briefly appeared' suggests a cameo; 'briefly' only clips SHE.
annotation.definitionFit: A pear-shaped figure is wider at the hips than the shoulders.

entries.clue: Comment on year in Italian art gallery (8)

blocks.note: the Tate, London's national art galleries

annotation.surface: A critic's note on a year spent at a gallery in Italy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian' attaches to 'year', not 'art gallery': the gallery is London's Tate.
annotation.definitionFit: To annotate a text is to add comments on it.

entries.clue: Hold up — connoisseur’s edited novel (8,6)

indicatorNotes.edited: the letters of connoisseur are reworked

blocks.note: to hold up a bank is to rob it

annotation.surface: A delay: an expert's revised novel is late.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' looks like a delay to publication; it is a robbery. The ’s is 'is', joining connoisseur to its indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe is Daniel Defoe's 1719 novel about a castaway.

entries.clue: Adjust movement from The Planets, no longer having quiet after loud one (4-4)

indicatorNotes.no longer having: what something no longer has it has lost, so NEPTUNE loses its P
indicatorNotes.after: NETUNE comes after F and I

blocks.clueFragment: movement from The Planets, no longer having quiet
blocks.note: Neptune, from Holst's suite, minus P (piano, quiet)

annotation.surface: An orchestra retunes a Holst movement, playing loud where it was once soft.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface supplies the conventions: p (piano) is quiet and f (forte) is loud. Neptune is the last movement of Holst's The Planets.
annotation.definitionFit: To fine-tune is to make small precise adjustments.

entries.clue: Church guarded by boy with added spirit? (5)

indicatorNotes.guarded by: guards stand around what they protect, so LAD stands around CE

annotation.surface: A church protected by a lad with holy zeal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests religious fervour beside the church; the question mark points to alcohol instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A drink is laced when spirits have been secretly added.

entries.clue: Unlawful activity close to Florida peninsula (6)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close, or last letter, of Florida

annotation.surface: Illegal goings-on near the Florida peninsula.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as 'near'; it means the final letter. Florida is itself a peninsula, a neat red herring.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Crimea juts into the Black Sea, joined to the mainland only by a narrow isthmus.

entries.clue: Bold sort of artist failing to get going after dawn (10)

indicatorNotes.after: what comes after something follows it in time, so URER follows ADVENT in the answer

blocks.note: an advent is an arrival or dawn of something
Albrecht Dürer, the German artist, minus his first letter

annotation.surface: A daring type of painter who can't start work after daybreak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bold sort of artist' seems one phrase; the definition stops at 'sort', and 'of' is the link.
annotation.definitionFit: An adventurer is a bold person who seeks risky experiences.

entries.clue: Running nicer hotel is better (6)

indicatorNotes.Running: the letters are run, set in motion

blocks.note: H = hotel in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A nicer hotel run is an improvement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective; it is a verb, to improve.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: enriching soil or a diet improves its quality.

entries.clue: Flying must upset pigs’ and swine’s eating (8,4)

indicatorNotes.upset: the letters of pigs and are overturned into a new order
indicatorNotes.eating: BOARS takes the mixed letters inside

annotation.surface: An absurd rule: pigs and swine will be upset at mealtime if they fly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pigs' and swine' look like one herd, but pigs and 'and' are the fodder while swine are the container. The surface nods to 'pigs might fly'.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-style definition: no passenger gets on a plane without this document, so it is a must for flying.

entries.clue: Noble, suppressing a small scream, produces toy weapon (10)

indicatorNotes.suppressing: PEER holds A S HOOT down inside

blocks.note: A + S (small) + HOOT (a scream, something hilarious)

annotation.surface: A lord stifles a little shriek and pulls out a toy gun.
annotation.walkthrough: A hoot and a scream are both slang for something very funny, so the 'scream' becomes HOOT.
annotation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a toy tube for blowing dried peas.

entries.clue: Sweetheart to hassle animal (5,6)

blocks.note: honey is a term of endearment

annotation.surface: Pestering one's darling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hassle' looks purely like a verb; as BADGER it also names half the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: The honey badger, or ratel, is a notoriously fearless African mammal.

entries.clue: Heartless official’s predicament (6)

indicatorNotes.Heartless: CORONER loses its middle letter, O

blocks.note: coroner, the official who investigates deaths, minus the central O

annotation.surface: An unfeeling bureaucrat is in a fix.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' reads as cruel; it means losing the central letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: being in a tight corner, or backed into one, means being in a fix with no easy way out.

entries.clue: Music producer, extremely snobby, with advanced degree? (5)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the extremes, first and last letters, of snobby

blocks.note: to the nth degree = to the utmost

annotation.surface: A very stuck-up record producer with a postgraduate qualification.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Advanced degree' suggests a PhD; the question mark signals the nth degree. 'Extremely' looks like 'very'.
annotation.definitionFit: A synth, or synthesiser, is an electronic instrument that produces music.

entries.clue: Transport part of gun — it may be needed in court (11)

annotation.definition: it may be needed in court

blocks.note: a shuttle is a transport service
the cock is a gun's hammer

annotation.surface: A firearm component taken to court as evidence.
annotation.walkthrough: The gun and 'court' suggest a trial; the court is a badminton court.
annotation.definitionFit: A shuttlecock is the feathered projectile needed to play badminton on a court.

entries.clue: Second lock put on delivery for comfort in anxiety (6,4)

indicatorNotes.put on: in a down answer S and TRESS sit on top of BALL

blocks.note: a lock of hair is a tress
in cricket each delivery is a ball

annotation.surface: A moment spent fixing a lock on a package brings calm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lock' and 'delivery' suggest a door and a parcel; they are hair and a cricket bowler's ball.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive: the squeezable foam toy is kneaded by worried people to calm their nerves.

entries.clue: Murder suspect colludes with matron for a change (7,7)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters; 'with' joins the two words

annotation.surface: A suspect plots with the hospital matron, for once.
annotation.walkthrough: Colonel Mustard is a suspect in Cluedo, the board game sold as Clue in North America.
annotation.definitionFit: Colonel Mustard is one of the six murder suspects in Cluedo.

entries.clue: A strip found below plumber’s second washer (9)

indicatorNotes.found below: in a down answer A UNDRESS comes under L
indicatorNotes.second: take the second letter of plumber

annotation.surface: A plumber's assistant replaces a tap washer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Washer' looks like the plumbing part; it is a person who washes clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman whose job is washing laundry.

entries.clue: Abandons Pixar film and prepares for operation (6,2)

blocks.note: to scrub a plan is to abandon it

annotation.surface: A studio cancels an animated film and gets ready for a business venture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Operation' reads as a project or campaign; it is surgery, and surgeons scrub up.
annotation.definitionFit: A surgeon scrubs up by washing thoroughly before operating.

entries.clue: Enthusiasm almost sent knees trembling (8)

indicatorNotes.trembling: the letters shake into a new order

annotation.surface: Passion so great it nearly left someone weak at the knees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sent' reads as thrilled, as in 'it really sent me'; it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone keen on a hobby is enthusiastic about it.

entries.clue: Delivered two letters later (3,3)

indicatorNotes.Delivered: the letters are delivered as speech, said out loud

blocks.note: C and U, the pair of letters texters use for a goodbye, spelt out as the words they are heard as

annotation.surface: A pair of letters will arrive in a later post.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests post and 'later' timing; it is the farewell, as 'later' and 'see you' both mean goodbye.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Later!' and 'See you!' are both casual ways of saying goodbye.

entries.clue: I announced ship’s paint (8)

indicatorNotes.announced: an announcement is heard rather than read, so I counts by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: I and eye sound the same
a liner is a passenger ship

annotation.surface: Someone proudly tells the world about their ship's paint job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paint' looks like a ship's coat of paint; it is make-up. The ’s is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is make-up painted along the eyelids.

entries.clue: Explicit broadcast’s finale shown in full (6)

indicatorNotes.shown in: something shown in a window sits inside it, so T sits inside SATED

annotation.surface: An X-rated programme's ending was shown uncut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Explicit broadcast' suggests adult content, and 'in full' uncut; the definition is 'Explicit' alone and 'full' is SATED.
annotation.definitionFit: Something explicit is stated plainly rather than implied.

entries.clue: Tech company beginning to trial program (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the first letter of trial

annotation.surface: A tech firm starts testing new software.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to trial' reads as starting a test; it only yields T.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: an applet is a small application, the -let suffix meaning little, as in booklet.

entries.clue: Sound system seen within austere office (6)

indicatorNotes.seen within: the answer is visible inside the next words

blocks.note: the letters run from the third letter of austere into the first of office

annotation.surface: A hi-fi spotted in a bare, strict workplace.
annotation.walkthrough: The austere office is exactly the place a stereo would look out of place.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a home stereo, short for stereophonic, is the hi-fi set that plays music through two speakers.

entries.clue: Pardons unruly prisoners for arguments? (4,3,4)

indicatorNotes.unruly: the letters of pardons are out of order

annotation.surface: An amnesty for rowdy inmates, and the debates it sparks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' seems to describe the prisoners; it rearranges pardons.
annotation.definitionFit: Pros and cons are the points for and against, from Latin pro and contra; the question mark flags the prisoner pun.

entries.clue: Energy of ducks on speed (5)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down answer OO sits on top of MPH

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

annotation.surface: Ducks high on amphetamines are full of beans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speed' suggests the drug; it is MPH. A duck is a zero score in cricket, giving O.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: a performance with oomph has zest and get-up-and-go.

entries.clue: Proprietor’s wife entering US city from the south (5)

indicatorNotes.entering: whoever enters a city ends up inside it, so W ends up inside the reversed RENO
indicatorNotes.from the south: in a down answer RENO reads upwards

annotation.surface: A businessman's wife arrives in an American city from the south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From the south' reads as a direction of travel; in a down clue it means reading upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the proprietor of a pub or shop is the person it belongs to.

entries.clue: New GP getting mixed up with heart and eye treatment (4,7)

indicatorNotes.getting mixed up: things that get mixed up lose their order, like shuffled papers, and so do these letters

annotation.surface: A newly qualified family doctor confuses heart care with eye care.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface suits the answer; GP (a family doctor) is just two letters in the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: Gene therapy is a medical treatment that alters a patient's genes.

entries.clue: Some money preserves site of battle (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: only part of the words is used
indicatorNotes.preserves: the phrase keeps the answer inside it

blocks.note: the letters run from the last letter of money into the first four of preserves

annotation.surface: A little cash protects a historic battlefield.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Preserves' does double duty, lending letters and signalling that the answer is kept inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Ypres in Belgium was the site of several First World War battles.

entries.clue: Foreign article admitting I’m naive? A shade! (4,5)

indicatorNotes.admitting: to admit someone is to let them in, so LE lets IM in between its letters

annotation.surface: A foreign reporter admits to naivety about a colour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a news piece; it is the grammatical article, French 'le'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the colour of lime peel is one particular shade.

entries.clue: Lay a floor cover by westbound French road (7)

indicatorNotes.by: EUR is placed beside A MAT
indicatorNotes.westbound: in an across answer RUE reads right to left

blocks.note: rue is French for street, reversed

annotation.surface: Instructions to put down a rug beside a French road heading west.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lay' reads as a verb, to put down; it is an adjective meaning non-professional, as in a lay preacher.
annotation.definitionFit: Lay and amateur both describe someone without professional training.

entries.clue: Additional relative skips Mass (5)

indicatorNotes.skips: to skip Mass is not to attend it, so M is not there in MOTHER

blocks.note: a mother is a relative; drop M, for mass

annotation.surface: Another family member misses church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service; it is M, the physics symbol for mass.
annotation.definitionFit: Other means additional, as in 'any other business'.

entries.clue: Mostly bad-tempered in reflective street clothes (1-6)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another is enclosed by it, so SHIRT is enclosed by TS
indicatorNotes.reflective: a reflection shows things back to front, as a mirror does, so ST reads as TS

blocks.note: shirty = bad-tempered in British slang, minus Y

annotation.surface: Grumpy people wearing hi-vis street gear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' suggests hi-vis clothing; it means mirrored. Shirty is British slang for irritable.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: T-shirts, named for their T shape when laid flat, are one everyday kind of clothes.

entries.clue: Costly car parts picked up (5)

indicatorNotes.picked up: heard, as a sound is picked up

annotation.surface: Expensive car components get collected.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Car parts' looks like one phrase; 'parts' means acting roles. A Rolls is short for a Rolls-Royce.
annotation.definitionFit: A Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, is a famously expensive car.

entries.clue: Store reportedly helps to make pens (9)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: the words are heard as spoken

blocks.note: a store of goods is stock
aids = helps, heard but spelt differently

annotation.surface: A shop is said to help with stationery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pens' suggests stationery in a store; it means enclosures.
annotation.definitionFit: Stockades are fenced enclosures, pens for animals or prisoners.
